info.title: Gauss pilot API
info.summary: The HTTP routes a Fleet Integration pilot calls: refined space-weather data and PR-01 trust records by organisation API key, organisation key and usage self-service by signed-in session, and the public health summary.
info.description:
Each operation states its access in `security` and in `x-gauss-access`:

- `/api/v1/*` (`api-key`): an organisation API key, `Authorization: Bearer gk_…`. Mounted before session auth (backend/commerce/routers.ts, createDataApiRouter). The organisation's plan must include API access; each key has a per-minute limit and each organisation a daily quota. Successful calls (status < 400) are metered by route template, never by query string.
- `/api/orgs/*` (`user`): a signed-in Gauss session with at least the `user` role (backend/rbac.ts, API_POLICY). The router also requires membership of the organisation; operators and admins may read any organisation's usage. Organisations, plans and members are managed by an admin with `npm run org`.
- `GET /health` (`public`): no credentials; `x-public-reason` says why.

Every `/api` request first passes CyberTiger, the server's intrusion guard. It answers 429 when the client IP is over its per-IP rate limit or blocked, and 400 when a request matches an attack signature, with `{ "error", "requestId" }`. Repeated 401 and 403 responses from one IP block that IP for a while, so fix credentials rather than retrying. Every `/api` response carries an `x-request-id` header; quote it when reporting a problem.

Unknown values are never filled with guesses: each schema says how it shows them (null, `unknown`, or quality flags on a carried-forward point). Fields may be added within 0.x; ignore fields you don't know.

Errors are JSON `{ "error": "…" }`. A request body that is not valid JSON is answered 400 `{ "error": "invalid JSON" }`, and one over 2 MB is answered 413. Both are answered before CyberTiger and before credentials are checked, so they carry no `x-request-id` and do not count toward the IP block.

Not covered: sign-in (`/api/auth/*`, served by better-auth); customer-log ingest and evidence packs (PR-03a and PR-04 are command-line tools, `npm run trust:ingest` and `npm run trust:verify`, with no HTTP routes); admin tooling. backend/commerce/openapi.test.ts fails if a pilot route and this file drift apart.

get.description: The newest point from the live feed. A point whose values were measured more than 15 minutes ago is still returned, but flagged stale (quality.stale and quality.lowConfidence true, quality.tier 3).

200.description: The latest point; check `quality` before treating its values as current

get.summary: Refined space-weather points over a lookback window

parameters.name: lookback
parameters.description: ISO 8601 duration with days, hours and minutes only (e.g. PT30M, PT6H, P1D). Defaults to PT1H; capped at the plan's maximum lookback. An unparseable value falls back to the default.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum points returned, clamped to 1..17280 (24 h at 5 s cadence).

200.description: Points, oldest first as provided by the history source

get.summary: Health of each upstream data source

post.summary: PR-01: a trust record for one inference, or a batch
post.description: Send one inference object, or {"inferences": [...]} with 1 to 100 items. Each item is validated on its own: in a batch, invalid items come back in `rejected` with their errors and are never guessed. Inference times older than the plan's lookback are refused (older windows are a replay pilot, PR-03). The environment is read from Gauss's held history at the inference time; records state their sources, ages, confidence and limitations. Every record returned is logged once (spacecraft and month) for invoicing before the response is sent; rejected items are not logged.

200.description: A single record (single request) or records plus rejected items (batch request)

400.description: The body was not valid JSON (`invalid JSON`), an invalid single inference (with `errors`), a batch outside 1..100 items, or CyberTiger refused the request (with `requestId`)

500.description: The usage log for invoicing could not be written, so no records were issued; safe to retry.

503.description: This server does not offer trust records (no environment history)

get.summary: Your organisations, their plan limits and API keys
get.description: Organisations the signed-in user is a member of, each with its plan limits and every API key it has had (active and revoked), oldest first. Keys are listed by prefix only; the secret is never shown again. An empty list when you are in no organisation: an admin adds members with `npm run org -- add-member`.

post.summary: Create an API key for your organisation
post.description: Members only. The plain key is in this response and nowhere else: Gauss stores only its SHA-256. Put it in a secret manager; never in a URL, a log or source control.

400.description: The body was not valid JSON (`invalid JSON`), or CyberTiger refused the request because it matched an attack signature (with `requestId`)

delete.summary: Revoke one of your organisation's API keys
delete.description: Members only. Takes effect at once: the next call with that key gets 401. Revoked keys stay listed, with revokedAt.

parameters.name: keyId
parameters.description: Key id (ApiKeyInfo.id), not the key itself

404.description: Not a member of the organisation, no such key in it, or the key was already revoked. No body.

get.summary: API calls per day, key and route for one organisation
get.description: Successful /api/v1 calls counted per UTC day, key and route template. Members see their organisation; operators and admins may read any. This counts calls: trust records per spacecraft-month, the pilot invoicing unit, come from the admin export `npm run org -- usage-csv`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First UTC day, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Missing or not in that shape: the first day of the current UTC month.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last UTC day, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Missing or not in that shape: today (UTC).

200.description: Usage rows; an empty list when there were no calls

get.description: For load balancers and monitoring. `npm run tpm` reads this and exits 0 (green or insufficient), 1 (amber), 2 (red) or 3 (unreachable). Outside /api, so CyberTiger does not inspect it. Measure values are behind `GET /api/system/tpm` (operator role, not a pilot route).
get.x-public-reason: Liveness for monitoring without credentials. It returns only the overall TPM status and the ids of red measures, never values, hosts or versions (backend/server.ts, GAU-122).

200.description: The process is up; judge health by tpm.status

apiKey.description: Organisation API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer gk_…`. Keys are created by organisation admins; never put a key in a URL.

session.name: better-auth.session_token
session.description: A signed-in Gauss session (better-auth). Sign in through the web app (email and password, or Google/GitHub single sign-on where the server enables it); the browser then sends the session cookie. better-auth's default cookie name is shown; on HTTPS origins it carries the `__Secure-` prefix. Machine integrations use an organisation API key instead; never copy a session cookie into scripts or logs.

QuotaRemaining.description: Requests left today after this one

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or revoked API key. Repeated 401s count towards CyberTiger's IP block.

PlanForbidden.description: The organisation's plan does not include API access

RateLimited.description: Per-key per-minute limit (with Retry-After) or the organisation's daily quota reached; or CyberTiger's per-IP limit or an IP block (the body then carries requestId)

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the minute window resets (minute limit only)

NoData.description: No data has been ingested yet

GuardRefused.description: CyberTiger refused the request because it matched an attack signature. Quote the requestId when reporting a false positive.

SessionRequired.description: No signed-in session (cookie missing or expired). Repeated 401s count towards CyberTiger's IP block.

GuardLimited.description: CyberTiger's per-IP rate limit, or the IP is blocked (for example after repeated 401 or 403 responses)

OrgNotFound.description: No such organisation, or you are not a member. The two look the same so organisation ids can't be probed.

BodyTooLarge.description: The request body was over 2 MB: `{ "error": "request body too large" }`. Send fewer items per request.

errors.description: Validation errors for a single trust-record request

requestId.description: CyberTiger request id, on requests it refused

SpaceWeatherPoint.description: One refined space-weather point, issued every 5 s (backend/types.ts CanonicalSpaceWeatherPoint). Vectors are GSM; plasma and field values come from the L1 monitor. How unknown values are shown: the core numbers (rho, velocity, magneticField, electricField, solarWind, indices, coupling) are never null. With no current L1 readout the point carries the previous values forward (or placeholders when there has never been a readout) and says so in `quality`: tier 1 = carried from a measurement still under the age cap, tier 3 = stale (stale and lowConfidence true). Treat tier-3 values as unknown, not as measurements. Optional enrichments are null when unknown or too old: arriving, densityCheck, xray, particles.protons, particles.electrons, noaaAlerts. A NOAA scale level of null means unknown, never 'no storm'; a sense check of `unknown` means nothing current to check, never 'pass'. Points from before a field existed (history after an upgrade) simply lack it.

timestamp.description: When the point was issued (5 s ingest tick), UTC

observedAt.description: When its L1 values were measured, UTC; freshness is judged from this. Null when there has been no measurement.

spacecraft.description: L1 spacecraft the values came from

rho.description: Proton number density, cm⁻³ (same as solarWind.density)

x.description: Motional electric field E = -V×B, mV/m, GSM

y.description: Motional electric field E = -V×B, mV/m, GSM

z.description: Motional electric field E = -V×B, mV/m, GSM

kp.description: Planetary Kp, 0 to 9; null when no source has a Kp reading (unknown, never a default value; GAU-230).

dstMethod.description: `measured` (Kyoto Dst under 2 h old), or the model that derived dst; a modelled Dst never passes for a measurement

dstDerivedFrom.description: Fields dst was derived from; empty when measured

kpKind.description: estimated-1m is current; planetary-3h lags up to 3 h

kpObservedAt.description: When the Kp value was observed, UTC

dstObservedAt.description: Hour of the measured Kyoto Dst; absent when dst is modelled

derived.description: Values not measured as published, with method and inputs; empty when all were measured

newell.description: Newell et al. (2007) coupling v^(4/3)·Bt^(2/3)·sin^(8/3)(θc/2), in (km/s)^(4/3)·nT^(2/3); compare values, not absolute units

epsilon.description: Akasofu ε energy input, W (l0 = 7 Re)

l1DelaySeconds.description: Ballistic L1-to-Earth travel time, s (1.5×10⁶ km at |Vx| clamped to 250–2000 km/s)

etaEarthArrival.description: When the measured solar wind reaches Earth, UTC

reason.description: Why, in words; ends with the Shue magnetopause standoff r0 in Re

radiation.description: NOAA S-scale from GOES ≥10 MeV protons

radioBlackout.description: NOAA R-scale from GOES 0.1–0.8 nm X-rays

arriving.description: Null until 3 h of L1 history covers one travel time, or when the feed is lost

densityCheck.description: Set when two L1 spacecraft disagree on density by more than 2×; the density uncertainty then spans both

xray.description: Null when missing or older than 15 min

protons.description: Null when missing or older than 30 min

electrons.description: Null when missing or older than 30 min

noaaAlerts.description: NOAA alerts, watches and warnings from the last 24 h, newest first; null when unreadable

stale.description: True when the values are past the age cap: treat as unknown

extrapolated.description: True when values were carried forward

tier.description: 0 live, 1 carried from a recent measurement, 2 synthetic, 3 stale (unknown)

level.description: 0 = below the scale; null = unknown (input missing or stale), never 'no storm'

label.description: e.g. S2 or G0; S? or G? when unknown

basis.description: What the level was read from, in words

observedAt.description: When the input was measured, UTC; null when there was none

status.description: `unknown` when there was nothing current to check, never `pass`

observedAt.description: Newest sample checked, UTC; null when there was none

checked.description: Samples checked, for checks over a window

flagged.description: Samples flagged, for checks over a window

derivedFrom.description: Published inputs it was obtained from

ArrivingSolarWind.description: The solar wind reaching Earth now: L1 values one ballistic travel time ago, 5-min mean, GSM

observedAt.description: Last L1 measurement in the mean, UTC

minutes.description: How long they have disagreed, min

headline.description: The line as NOAA wrote it

source.description: Which history served the points. `memory` is the backend's in-memory feed (about 28 h at 5 s cadence, reloaded from local telemetry on restart).

lookbackMs.description: Lookback actually applied, after the plan cap

lastSeen.description: Last successful fetch, UTC; null when never

message.description: Why it is unhealthy, when it is

altKm.description: Altitude above the reference ellipsoid, km

output.description: The model output, any JSON of at most 4096 bytes (UTF-8)

tle.description: Two-line element set; the spacecraft position is propagated with SGP4 when no ephemeris is given

Field.description: One context value with its provenance. `value` is null when unknown and `limitations` says why.

fetchedAt.description: Issue time of the reading Gauss held

TrustRecord.description: backend/trust/record.ts TrustRecord. `hash` is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the record without `hash`.

ingest.description: Present when the inference came from an ingested customer log (PR-03); null over the API

environmentSource.description: Which history the environment was read from

particleFlux.description: Nearest-available proxy: GOES ≥10 MeV integral protons, pfu

fieldStrength.description: IGRF-14 total field intensity at the position, nT

upsetRisk.description: Modelled upset-risk band; unknown without a cited processor profile (PR-02)

Plan.description: What an organisation has bought (backend/commerce/plans.ts); set by an admin

api.description: Whether the organisation's keys may call /api/v1 at all

requestsPerDay.description: Per organisation, all keys together, per UTC day

maxLookbackMs.description: Longest history window and oldest trust-record inference time, ms

ApiKeyInfo.description: An API key's metadata. The secret itself is never returned after creation.

prefix.description: Tells keys apart in lists; not enough to use the key

createdBy.description: User id of the member who created it

lastUsedAt.description: Last successful call; null when never used

revokedAt.description: Null while the key is active

name.description: A label for the key; trimmed and cut to 80 characters. Empty or missing: "API key".

key.description: The API key. Shown once; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

rows.description: Ordered by day, key and endpoint

ok.description: Always true when the process answers

status.description: Worst technical performance measure (backend/lib/tpm.ts). `insufficient`: a measure has no value yet (for example just after start); it never hides amber or red.
